test_title: PYST 1: SSC CGL 2025 - General Knowledge (Held On: 12th_September_2025_Shift_1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is true about Fundamental Rights and DPSPs?

options.text: Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts
DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict
Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not
DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution;Fundamental Rights are optional

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are explicitly mentioned in Part III of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their rights are violated. This makes them **justiciable**.
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs)**, enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution, are not enforceable by the courts, making them **non-justiciable**.
 
• DPSPs act as guidelines for the government to achieve socio-economic goals and establish a welfare state.
 
• While **Fundamental Rights** focus on individual rights and liberties, DPSPs emphasize **collective welfare** and societal development.
 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has clarified that Fundamental Rights and DPSPs must be harmonized and not seen as conflicting entities.
 
• Examples of Fundamental Rights include the **Right to Equality** (Article 14-18) and the **Right to Freedom** (Article 19-22).
 
• Examples of DPSPs include the directive to promote **equal justice** and free legal aid (Article 39A) and to ensure **living wages** for workers (Article 43).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Both are justiciable and enforceable by courts**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **only Fundamental Rights** are enforceable by courts, while DPSPs are not.
 
• DPSPs serve as principles for governance and cannot be legally upheld in courts.
 
 
 
• **DPSPs override Fundamental Rights when in conflict**__
 __
 
• The **Supreme Court** has ruled that Fundamental Rights hold a higher position in cases of conflict.
 
• However, efforts have been made to harmonize both, recognizing their complementary nature.
 
 
 
• **DPSPs are guaranteed by the Constitution; Fundamental Rights are optional**__
 
 
• This is incorrect as both Fundamental Rights and DPSPs are integral parts of the Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Rights are guaranteed and enforceable, while DPSPs are guidelines that cannot be enforced legally.
